name: Weighing the Scientific Consensus
title: Weighing the Scientific Consensus
answer: Weighing the scientific consensus means assessing how much agreement exists across published AI research on a given question, and how strong that agreement is. It covers both formal meta-analyses and lighter structured reviews that compare findings, effect directions, and methodological quality. The site's library of 135 research papers and 10,767 extracted claims provides a bounded corpus for this kind of work. The goal is to separate findings that are robust across many studies from those that rest on a single result or a contested method.

sections.body: Weighing the scientific consensus means assessing how much agreement exists across published AI research on a given question, and how strong that agreement is. It covers both formal meta-analyses and lighter structured reviews that compare findings, effect directions, and methodological quality. The site's library of 135 research papers and 10,767 extracted claims provides a bounded corpus for this kind of work. The goal is to separate findings that are robust across many studies from those that rest on a single result or a contested method.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The work runs on a curated document store of original papers and books, with claims extracted into a structured database that records the source, the claim text, and the study context. The site's catalogue of 91 AI books and 674 glossary terms supports interpretation, but the core infrastructure is the claim-to-paper linkage. No external consensus search tool is used; every extracted claim resolves to the original paper so that a reader can verify the context. This keeps the evidence chain short and auditable.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: Analysts read papers and extract discrete, testable claims, then code each claim for direction, strength, and the type of evidence behind it. The 10,767 claims extracted from research works are compared across studies to see where findings converge, diverge, or remain untested. Where quantitative results are comparable, simple vote counting or effect direction plots are used; where they are not, the synthesis is narrative and focuses on conditions and caveats. The method treats a consensus as provisional, not as proof.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Provenance is the main control: content on this site never links to the Consensus search tool; it links to the original paper. This reduces the risk of a claim being stripped of its methods, sample, or limitations. The main risks are selective citation, publication bias toward positive results, and the temptation to treat a numerical majority as scientific truth. Reviewers are expected to flag disagreement and low-quality evidence rather than smooth it over.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: The practice is moving toward living evidence maps that update as new papers are added, so a consensus estimate can shift without a full manual re-review. Better claim extraction and contradiction detection may make it easier to see where the field is split. The likely outcome is less emphasis on a single headline answer and more on the distribution of evidence, including the size and quality of studies behind each side.
